newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh to offload public shares.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh to offload public shares.

text.p: Bangladesh's Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) chief said on Thursday that the government was offloading public shares to beef up the country's stock market.

"The government as a first step will privatise the companies which are already listed with the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) to increase the market depth," SEC Chairman Haroonur Rashid told Reuters in an interview.

He said the government would sell its stakes in all multinational companies, which number about eight. The government's shares in Reckitt & Colman (BD) Ltd, listed on the DSE have been sold, he said. It also has sold its shares in British-linked Bangladesh Tobacco Company Ltd.
"I hope offloading of shares in all these multinationals will be completed by December," he said.
Rashid said Bangladesh was planning to sell 2.0 billion taka worth of shares in state-owned companies listed on the DSE by the end of fiscal 1996/97 (July-June).
"But it all depends on how speedily the government can privatise public companies," he said.
He added: "We are pressuring the government to privatise all the state-owned enterprises.
Rashid said there had been an "encouraging response" from private sector companies to go public after the new government took over in June this year.

He said four companies released Initial Public Offering (IPOs) worth 540 million taka this month and another four were being ready to enter the market. "We have given permission to 14 new companies to float public shares since July," he added.
Rashid expects 50 more companies to release IPOs by next July.

"There is pressure on the market due to a shortage of securities in market. But lack of knowledge is also fuelling the share prices," he said, referring to hundreds of retail investors chasing too few stocks.
The benchmark DSE index reached an all-time high of 2,823.62 points on Wednesday, having climbed in four days from 2,193.8 last Thursday. Friday is the weekend in Moslem Bangladesh.
Market capitalisation has risen to $4.71 billion on Wednesday from $2.84 billion on October 2. It was only $452 million at the end of 1994.

Brokers said the surge continued despite an SEC warning against trading in 24 losing companies, transactions in the kerb market and news of a price movement limit of 10 percent of the previous day's rate, in effect since October 10.
The SEC chairman said the Dhaka Stock Exchange should move towards computerised trading for transparency and accountability. "Automation is a must and a priority," he said.

He said there might have been cases of market manipulation behind the sharp rise in stock prices. "Intermediaries (brokers) are not also playing their role. The retail investors should be educated before staking their hard-earned money," he said.
